doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: Austin Cromer, Esther Phillips and other early sideman dates
summary: Brown reads through sideman sessions for Austin Cromer, Esther Phillips and Solomon Ilori. Laws recalls little and explains how producers used label artists as sidemen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: It’s got every date, at least every date they were able to identify, and there are 333 entries. The next ones are with Esther Phillips, with the Ray Ellis orchestra.
That’s right. I did another one, a guy named Austin Cromer. You got it.
Yeah. That was earlier. I didn’t mention – do you want me to go back and list it?

No, because I don’t remember anything about it. See, the thing is, I just remember his name, Austin Cromer, and I remember Esther, because they were – I think they did that for Atlantic Records. See, these guys put me on those sessions, because, I guess, just like what Creed did. He began having his artists to participate on other artists in his corral, the label, their records.
Yeah, because Chick is on that Austin Cromer.
He is?
Yeah, Chick was on it, Richard Davis. So yeah, like I said, this is indispensible. Lyle Atkinson on bass. Bobby Capers.
Yeah, I know Lyle. Lyle used to be on those Latin bands that we played. Yeah, Lyle Atkinson. I wonder if he’s still around?
I can find out and let you know tomorrow.
Well, I can too. I probably could go on line.
Yeah. Then, the Esther Phillips date: how was that? Esther singing. This is your first vocal – led by a vocalist.

I don’t remember, Anthony. I just – I remember I did the date, but I just don’t recall. I know I did some solos in there. There were little spots for me to play solos here and there. Esther Phillips also is from my home town. They used to call her Little Esther.
Right, right. I know, because of Johnny Otis. They have a lot of Mongo, and then Solomon De ? How do you pronounce that? Do you remember that?
Who?
Solomon – it’s I-l-o-r-i. It had Elvin Jones on it. That’s what caught my eye.
I played on that?
Um-hmm.
I don’t recall that one.
Flute and tenor sax.
I don’t recall.
It was just a couple. So it was probably a studio – you probably got called to the studio. Then back to Sergio Mendes. That might have been the same album. They just – there was a different session.
